title: Fourth moment bound for linear forms
statement: For every natural number $n$ and every coefficient vector $a\in\mathbb{R}^n$, let $X$ be uniform on $\{-1,1\}^n$ and put $L_a(X)=\sum_{i=1}^n a_iX_i$. Then $\mathbb{E}[L_a(X)^4]\le 3\bigl(\mathbb{E}[L_a(X)^2]\bigr)^2$.
hypotheses_covered: $a$ is an arbitrary real coefficient vector indexed by $n$ coordinates
The distribution on the Boolean cube is uniform
